question: Post-polio residual paralysis produces flaccid, hypotonic paralysis with areflexia because the poliovirus selectively destroys lower motor neurones in the anterior horn of the spinal cord.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. PPRP is a classic LMN disorder. Anterior horn cell destruction removes the final common pathway; the result is flaccid, wasted, areflexic muscle — not spasticity. Only UMN lesions (e.g., CP) produce spasticity.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Poliovirus is an LMN lesion: it destroys anterior horn cells, producing flaccid paralysis, wasting, hypotonia, and absent deep tendon reflexes — the opposite of the UMN spasticity seen in cerebral palsy.
